nTop · Geometry report · Revision 5

A smoother fuselage.
The B-52F shape retained.

The new loft removes barrel ripples and softens the tail transition while retaining the cockpit profile.

10 SEP 2026PREPARED FOR: BRAD ROTHENBERGR5 · NATIVE NTOP VERIFIED

Measured result

The barrel spline has no curvature reversals. All three geometric silhouettes remain above 99%.

R4 had continuous second derivatives, but its section curvature still oscillated. R5 reduces the transverse controls from 28 to 16 and applies convex-section constraints. Stronger longitudinal fairing removes the abrupt tail changes.

Derived geometric agreement with the selected public B-52F artist model. These scores do not establish production-aircraft accuracy.

01 / SURFACE FAIRNESSRemove the ripples in the shape.

The main barrel spline had seven curvature sign changes in R4. The revised spline has zero. Its curvature variation falls by 72.6%. C2 continuity alone did not guarantee a fair surface.

R5 / REFINED

The local nose and cockpit comparison remains above 99%: 99.705% plan and 99.222% side. The forward underside stays free of the previously rejected lump.

02 / SHAPE VERIFICATIONKeep the independent benchmark.

The frozen public model, clean-skin scope, coordinate frame, and scale are unchanged from R4. The study length is 9.144 m. The comparison uses the complete frozen source contours, including differences at the gear recesses and tail housing.

IoU is shared silhouette area divided by combined silhouette area. It uses the final saved spline definition, with the native crown, keel, and width clips. The final integration uses 4,097 longitudinal and 513 transverse samples. Scores measure continuous geometry, not viewport pixels. Window annotations are excluded. The earlier detached crown artifact is absent in the R5 native front render.

R5 retains the native Notebook API loft graph and updates its control net. nTop Automate evaluates the final native field probes. No fresh Notebook API readback is claimed for this revision.
